members.name: Three members of Stone Temple Pilots (excluding Scott Weiland)

podcast.title: Therapeutic for Band Members (1998)
podcast.body: The other Stone Temple Pilots members found the process of making the "Talk Show" record to be "therapeutic" for them, much like Scott Wyland found his solo album therapeutic. This experience taught them valuable lessons, particularly about their chemistry and mutual importance. "I think after the talk show thing, I think the talk show record was really therapeutic for all of us to make."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Artistic Underperformance
podcast.body: The band was considered a "disaster" and demonstrated that its members were "merely competent rock band" without Scott Weiland, especially when compared to Weiland's solo artistic output. "While Talk Show demonstrated that they were a merely competent rock band, Wyland's record showed that he had something that made STP special."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-STP Project
podcast.body: Formed by the instrumental members of Stone Temple Pilots after their split with Scott Weiland in 1997. "The other three guys formed a group called Talk Show".

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: STP Hiatus Project
podcast.body: During a hiatus of Stone Temple Pilots in 1998, which was intended to help Scott Weiland with his issues, the other three members (Dean DeLeo, Robert DeLeo, and Eric Kretz) formed a new project called Talk Show with singer David Coutts. This project "did not work out very well," leading to the original STP lineup reuniting. "At that point, the other three quarters of STP formed a new project called Talk Show with the singer named David Coots, which did not work out very well and STP was tuned back together in its original form."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Bill Grundy Interview (1976)
xref.body: On December 1, 1976, the Sex Pistols appeared on Bill Grundy's afternoon talk show as last-minute substitutes. The band arrived drunk and surly, leading to an infamous on-air interview filled with obscenities. This controversial broadcast, likened to the "Janet Jackson Nipplegate scandal of its day," transformed the Sex Pistols from mere curiosities into national and international sensations.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Cancelled TV Appearance (December 1, 1976)
xref.body: Queen was scheduled to be a guest on Bill Grundy's "Today" talk show on ITV on December 1, 1976. However, they had to cancel at the last minute, reportedly because Freddie Mercury needed to be rushed to the dentist for a bad toothache. Their cancellation led to the Sex Pistols being invited as a last-minute replacement. "But at the last second they had to cancel. Everybody seems to recall it was because somebody in the band needed to be rushed to the dentist with a bad toothache. I think it was Freddie Mercury."

xref.title: Hiatus and Talk Show Project (1998)
xref.body: In 1998, the band went on a hiatus aimed at helping Scott Weiland get clean. During this break, the other three members formed a new project called Talk Show with singer David Coutts, which ultimately "did not work out very well," leading to STP's reunion in its original form. "At that point, the other three quarters of STP formed a new project called Talk Show with the singer named David Coots, which did not work out very well and STP was tuned back together in its original form."

xref.title: Artistic Success Compared to Former Bandmates
xref.body: Artistically, Weiland's solo record, 12 Bar Blues, was considered superior to the efforts of his former Stone Temple Pilots bandmates in Talk Show, demonstrating that he possessed a unique quality that made STP special. "Artistically, the winner in this battle was Scott Wyland. I mean, it wasn't even close."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Career Hit and Rebound
xref.body: DeGeneres' career took a hit after the cancellation of her show. However, she rebounded in 2003 by portraying Dory the forgetful fish in *Finding Nemo* and launching her hugely successful talk show, *The Ellen DeGeneres Show*, in the same year. "DeGeneres' career took a hit after the cancellation of her show, but she rebounded in 2003 when she portrayed Dory the forgetful fish in Finding Nemo."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Drummer to Talk Show Host
xref.body: Jenny Jones, originally a runaway from London, Ontario, became a drummer for an all-girl band called The Cover Girls in Los Angeles. She was later discovered by Wayne Newton, which led her to gigs in Las Vegas, eventually transitioning to become the host of the daytime talk show, The Jenny Jones Show, in the 1990s. "Jenny Jones was a runaway from London, Ontario, who ended up in L.A. playing drums for an all-girl band called The Cover Girls."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Career in Stand-up
xref.body: She began performing comedy routines at coffee shops in New Orleans in the late 1970s and early 1980s. Like other aspiring comedians, she moved to Los Angeles to perform on the circuit there. "The talk show host began performing her comedy routines at coffee shops in the late 70s and early 80s in New Orleans."

xref.title: Hurley Album Cover Model
xref.body: Jorge Garcia, who played the character Hurley in the TV series "Lost," is featured on the cover of Weezer's "Hurley" album. The image is a cropped picture of Rivers Cuomo hugging Garcia in the green room of the late-night talk show "Lopez Tonight," where both were guests. "That's Jorge Garcia, a guy you played early on the show on the cover."

xref.title: Talk Show Allegations (Current)
xref.body: As of the time of recording, the future of *The Ellen DeGeneres Show* is uncertain, with investigations taking place by the network following allegations of abuse from a number of former and current employees. "But as of this recording, the future of the talk show is up in the air."

xref.title: Three Singers Post-Weiland – Chester Bennington Moonlighted from Linkin Park; Jeff Gutt Won Online Audition
xref.body: Scott Weiland was fired and rehired multiple times; the first replacement attempt involved David Coutts in a short-lived side project called Talk Show that failed entirely. Weiland was fired for good in 2013; he died of a drug overdose in 2016 without reconciling with the band. Chester Bennington of Linkin Park — a lifelong STP fan — was brought in for approximately two and a half years, was made an official member, toured, and recorded two tracks before returning to Linkin Park. His replacement was Jeff Gutt, found through an online audition that also briefly considered John Borja from the Philippines; Gutt had been a runner-up on Season 3 of *The X Factor* and was confirmed by fall 2017. "Chester was also a lifelong STP fan since, well, since he could remember."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
